nodes.name: Case (A), $w'=0$: yields the families of $\eqref{eq:sol1}$ and $\eqref{eq:sol2}$
nodes.statement:
\subsubsection{Case \underline{$w' =0$}.} Then  egin{equation} 2 a_3= u' a_1 + v' a_2 	ext{ with } v' \in \{0, 1\}. \end{equation} If $v'=1$, then $2 a_3= u' a_1+ a_2$, with $u' \geq 1$. Adding to this the equation \eqref{eq:case-a}, after obvious simplifications we obtain $a_2+a_3= (u+u')a_1$, hence $$ a_5=(a_2+a_3+a_4)-a_1= (u+u'-1) a_1+a_4 \in \langle a_1, a_4angle, $$ which is false. Thus $v'=0$ and $2 a_3= u' a_1$ where $u'>1$ need to be odd and $a_1$ even. Together with \eqref{eq:case-a} this gives $2(2a_2-u a_1)= u' a_1$, i.e. $$ 4 a_2= (u'+2u) \cdot a_1. $$ Since $u'$ is odd we get $4| a_1$, hence $a_1 \in \{ 8, 12 \}$.  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm,label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$a_1=8$}, then $$ egin{matrix} a_2 &=& 2(u'+2u),\ a_3 &=& 2 a_2- u a_1= 4u' . \end{matrix}$$ Consider the normalized expression \eqref{eq:a4-normalized}: $$ 2a_4= u'' a_1 + v'' a_2 + w'' a_3 +\lambda'' a_5. $$ If $\lambda''=1$, since $a_1, a_2, a_3$ are even, then $a_5$ is even. Using \eqref{eq:sum} we infer that $a_4$ is even, which is false. Therefore $\lambda''=0$ and $$2a_4= u'' a_1 + v'' a_2 + w'' a_3. $$ Since $a_2, a_3<a_4$ we should have $u''>0$. Because $4|a_1$ and $4|a_3$, we can not have $v''=0$, otherwise $a_4$ is even, and by \eqref{eq:sum} also $a_5$ is even, which gives a contradiction. Hence $v''=1$. We distinguish two situations.  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm, label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$w''=1$}, then $2 a_4= u'' a_1 + a_2+ a_3$. This gives  egin{eqnarray} a_1 &=& 8, 
onumber \ a_3 &=& 4u', 
onumber \ a_2 &=& 4u+2u', \ a_4 &=& 4u''+ 2u+ 3u', 
onumber\ a_5 &=& 9u'+6u+4u''-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} which is of the desired form. \item If \underline{$w''=0$}, then $2 a_4= u'' a_1 + a_2$. This gives  egin{eqnarray} a_1 &=& 8, 
onumber \ a_3 &=& 4u', 
onumber \ a_2 &=& 4u+2u', \ a_4 &=& 4u''+ 2u+ u', 
onumber\ a_5 &=& 7u'+6u+4u''-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} which is of the desired form. \end{enumerate} \item If \underline{$a_1=12$}, then  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=& 3u'+ 6u,\ a_3 &=& 6u'. \end{eqnarray*} In the normalized expression $$ \quad 2a_4= u'' a_1 + v'' a_2 + w'' a_3 +\lambda'' a_5 $$ we add $a_4+(1-v'') a_2+ (1-w'')a_3$ to both sides and using \eqref{eq:sum} we get $$ 3 a_4 +(1-v'')a_2+(1-w'')a_3= (1+u'')a_1+ (1+\lambda'')a_5, $$ hence $3|a_5$, and by \eqref{eq:sum} also $3|a_4$, hence $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_5) >1$, a contradiction. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $w'=0$ one gets $2a_3=u'a_1$, forcing $4\mid a_1$, and $a_1=8$ produces the two solution families while $a_1=12$ contradicts $\gcd=1$.

nodes.name: Case (A), $w'=1$: yields the family of $\eqref{eq:sol3}$
nodes.statement:
\subsubsection{Case \underline{$w'=1$}.} Then  egin{equation*} 2a_3= u' a_1+ v' a_2+a_4 	ext{ with } v'\in \{0,1\}. \end{equation*} If $v'=1$, then $2a_1+ 2a_5= 2a_2+ 2a_3+ 2 a_4= (u a_1+a_3)+ (u' a_1+ a_2+a_4)+ 2a_4= (u'+u) a_1+ (a_2+a_3+a_4)+ 2a_4$. This gives $a_5=(u'+u-1)a_1+2 a_4$, which is false. 
oindent Therefore $v'=0$ and  egin{equation} 2a_3= u' a_1+ a_4 	ext{ with } u' >0. \end{equation} Consider the normalized expression \eqref{eq:a4-normalized}  egin{equation*} 2a_4= u'' a_1 + v'' a_2 + w'' a_3 +\lambda'' a_5. \end{equation*} If $\lambda'' =1$, since $u''\lambda''=0$, we get $u''=0$. Equation \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} becomes  egin{equation*} 2 a_4= v'' a_2+ w'' a_3+ a_5. \end{equation*} To this we add \eqref{eq:a3} and $2a_2= u a_1+a_3$ from \eqref{eq:case-a} and after using \eqref{eq:sum} we get that $$ a_5= (u'+u-2) a_1 + v'' a_2+ (w''+1) a_3+ a_4 \in \langle a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4angle, $$ which is false. 
oindent Thus $\lambda''=0$ and $$ 2 a_4= u'' a_1+ v'' a_2+ w'' a_3. $$ To this we add \eqref{eq:a3} and $2a_2= u a_1+a_3$ and, after using \eqref{eq:sum}, we see that $$ 2 a_5=(u''+u'+u-2) a_1+ v'' a_2+ (w''+1)a_3+ a_4. $$ If $v''>0$, by \eqref{eq:sum} we get $a_5\in \langle a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 angle$, which is false. 
oindent Hence $v''=0$ and \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} becomes $$ 2a_4= u'' a_1+ w'' a_3= u'' a_1+ w''(2a_2-u a_1)= (u''-w''u)a_1+ 2w'' a_2 	ext{ with } w''\in\{0, 1\}. $$ From \eqref{eq:a3} we extract $$ a_4= 2a_3-u' a_1= 2(2a_2-u a_1)- u' a_1=4a_2-(2u+u')a_1 $$ which we replace in the previous equation for $2a_4$. Routine manipulation gives  egin{equation} (8-2w'')a_2=((4-w'')u+2u'+u'') a_1. \end{equation}  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm,label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$w''=0$}, the equations \eqref{eq:combo}, \eqref{eq:case-a} and \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} together with \eqref{eq:sum} yield  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=&  rac{4u+2u'+u''}{8} \cdot a_1, \ a_3 &=&  rac{2u'+u''}{4} \cdot a_1, \ a_4 &=&  rac{u''}{2} \cdot a_1,\ a_5 &=&  rac{4u+6u'+7u''-8}{8} \cdot a_1. \end{eqnarray*} From here we infer that $u''$ is odd (otherwise $a_1$ divides $a_4$, which is false) and consequently $8|a_1$. Hence $a_1=8$ and the generators of the semigroup are  egin{eqnarray} a_1 &=& 8, 
onumber \ a_4 &=& 4u'', 
onumber \ a_3 &=& 2u''+4u', \ a_2 &=& u''+ 2u'+ 4u, 
onumber \ a_5 &=& 4u+6u'+ 7u''-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} as desired. \item If \underline{$w''=1$}, equation \eqref{eq:combo} together with \eqref{eq:case-a}, \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} and \eqref{eq:sum} give after routine computations  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=&  rac{3u+2u'+u''}{6} \cdot a_1, \ a_3 &=&  rac{2u'+u''}{3} \cdot a_1, \ a_4 &=&  rac{u'+2u''}{3} \cdot a_1,\ a_5 &=&  rac{3u+8u'+7u''-6}{6} \cdot a_1. \end{eqnarray*} We note that $a_5= a_2+ (u'+u''-1) a_1 \in \langle a_1, a_2 angle$, which is false. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $w'=1$ the relations collapse to $(8-2w'')a_2=((4-w'')u+2u'+u'')a_1$; $w''=0$ gives a third solution family and $w''=1$ is impossible.

nodes.name: Case (B): $2a_2 = u a_1 + a_4$ and $\lambda''=0$
nodes.statement: \subsection{\underline{Case (B)}} Assume \begin{equation} 2 a_2= u a_1 + a_4, \text{ with }u \geq 1. \end{equation} If in the normalized expression $$ 2 a_4= u'' a_1+ v'' a_2+ w'' a_3+\lambda'' a_5 \text{\quad with } v'', w'', \lambda'' \in\{0,1\} $$ we had $\lambda''=1$, then $u''=0$. Combined with \eqref{eq:case-b}, we get $$ 2a_2+a_4= ua_1+ 2 a_4= u a_1 +v'' a_2 +w''a_3+a_5. $$ Using \eqref{eq:sum} and the latter equation we obtain $$ (1-v'')a_2= (u-1)a_1+ (w''+1) a_3 >0, $$ which is a contradiction since $v'' \leq 1$. Therefore $\lambda''=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Open the second branch $2a_2=ua_1+a_4$ and rule out $\lambda''=1$.

nodes.name: Case (B), $w'=v'=0$: yields the family of $\eqref{eq:sol4}$
nodes.statement:
\subsubsection{Case \underline{$w'=v'=0$}.} Then $u'>0$ and \eqref{eq:a3-normalized} becomes  egin{equation} 2 a_3= u' a_1. \end{equation} From this and \eqref{eq:case-b} we get $a_3=u'a_1/2$, $a_4=2a_2-u a_1$ and that $a_1$ is even and $u'$ is odd. We substitute in the normalized expression above the values for $a_3$ and $a_4$ in terms of $a_1$ and $a_2$ and we get $$ (4-v'') \cdot a_2= \left(2u+u''+ w'' rac{u'}{2}ight) \cdot a_1. $$  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm,label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$v''=1$}, the previous equation becomes $$ 3a_2= \left(2u+u''+w'' rac{u'}{2}ight) \cdot a_1. $$ We consider the possible even values of $a_1$.  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm, label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$a_1=6$} we obtain the other generators  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=& 4u+2u''+w''u',\ a_3 &=& 3u', \ a_4 &=&2u+4u''+2w''u', \ a_5 &=& 6u+6u''+ (3w''+3)u'-6. \end{eqnarray*} Note that $a_5 = (u+u''-1) a_1+ (w''+1) a_3\in \langle a_1, a_3 angle$, which is false. \item If \underline{$a_1=8$ or $12$}, then $a_2,a_3, a_4$ are even, hence $a_5$ is even as well, a contradiction. \item If \underline{$a_1=10$}, then it easy to see that $a_2,a_3, a_4, a_5$ are divisible by $5$, which is false. \item If \underline{$a_1=14$}, then all the generators are divisible by $7$, which is false. \end{enumerate} \item If \underline{$v''=0$}, then $$ 4a_2= \left(2u+u''+w'' rac{u'}{2}ight)\cdot a_1, $$ which forces $a_1$ to be even.  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm, label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$w''=0$} we get $2 a_4= u'' a_1$ and $4 a_2= (2u+u'') a_1$. Therefore $u''$ is odd, $a_1$ is divisible by $4$, hence $a_1\in \{4,8\}$, and the other generators are  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=&  rac{2u+u''}{4}\cdot a_1,\ a_3 &=&  rac{u'}{2}\cdot a_1, \ a_5 &=&  rac{3u''+2u+2u'-4}{4}\cdot a_1. \end{eqnarray*} It is immediate to note that if $a_1=8$ all generators are even, while if $a_1=12$ all of them are divisible by $3$. None of these situations may hold. \item If \underline{$w''=1$} we obtain $$ 8 a_2= (4u+2u''+u') \cdot a_1. $$ Since $u'$ is odd we get $a_1=8$. From the other equations we compute the other generators  egin{eqnarray} a_3 &=& 4u', 
onumber\ a_4 &=& 4u''+2u', 
onumber \ a_2 &=& 4u+ 2u''+u', \ a_5 &=& 4u+6u''+7u'-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} which turn out to be of the desired form. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $w'=v'=0$ all even values $a_1=6,8,10,12,14$ are excluded except $a_1=8$ with $v''=0,w''=1$, giving a fourth family.

nodes.name: Case (B), $w'=0$ and $v'=1$: yields the family of $\eqref{eq:sol5}$
nodes.statement:
\subsubsection{Case \underline{$w'= 0$ and $v'=1$}.} Then $2 a_3= u'a_1+a_2$ with $u'>0$. Using \eqref{eq:case-b} and the normalized equation \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} we get $$ 2a_1+ 2a_5= 2 a_2+ 2a_3+ 2a_4=(u'+u''+u)a_1+ (v''+1) a_2+ w'' a_3+ a_4, $$ hence $w''=0$.  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm,label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$v''=1$}, by adding the equations $2a_2=u a_1+ a_4$ and $2a_4= u'' a_1+ a_2$ we get $a_2+a_4=(u+u'')a_1$. Therefore $a_5=(a_2+a_4)+ a_3-a_1= (u+u''-1) a_1+a_3$, which is false. \item If \underline{$v''=0$}, then $2a_4=u'' a_1$ with $u''$ odd and $a_1$ even. Since $2a_2=u a_1+ a_4$ we get $4 a_2= (2u+ u'')\cdot a_1$. This implies that $4|a_1$, hence $a_1\in \{8,12\}$. If \underline{$a_1=12$}, then $a_2=3(2u+u'')$. Since $2 a_3=u' a_1+ a_2$ and $a_4= ua_1-2a_2$ we derive that $a_3$ and $a_4$ are divisible by $3$, hence also $3|a_5$, which is false. If \underline{$a_1=8$}, the rest of the generators are  egin{eqnarray} a_4 &=& 4u'', 
onumber \ a_2 &=& 4u+2u'', 
onumber \ a_3 &=& 2u+u''+4u', \ a_5 &=& 6u+7u''+4u'-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} which are of the desired format. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Here $w''=0$, $v''=1$ is contradictory and $v''=0$ forces $a_1=8$, giving a fifth family.

nodes.name: Case (B), $w'=1$: yields the family of $\eqref{eq:sol6}$
nodes.statement:
\subsubsection{Case \underline{$w'=1$}.} Then  egin{equation} 2a_3=u' a_1+ v' a_2+a_4. \end{equation} Since in the normalized expression \eqref{eq:a4-normalized} we have $\lambda''=0$ and $v'',w'' \leq 1$, then $u'' >0$. 
oindent By \eqref{eq:case-b} and \eqref{eq:new-new-a3} we may write  egin{eqnarray*} 2 a_5 &=& 2a_2+ 2a_3+2a_4-2a_1 \ &=& (u a_1+a_4) + (u'a_1+v' a_2 +a_4) + (u''a_1+v''a_2+w'' a_3)-2a_1 \ &=& (u+u'+u''-2) a_1+ (v'+v'')a_2 +w'' a_3 +2a_4. \end{eqnarray*}  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm,label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$w''=1$ and $v'+v'' >0$}, we get $a_5 \in \langle a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 angle$, which is false. \item If \underline{$w''=1$ and $v'=v''=0$}, summing the equations  egin{eqnarray*} 2a_4 &=& u'' a_1+ a_3 \ 2 a_3 &=& u' a_1 +a_4 \end{eqnarray*} we obtain that $a_3+a_4=(u'+u'')a_1$, which, together with \eqref{eq:sum} yields $a_5=(u'+u''-1)a_1+a_2 \in \langle a_1, a_2 angle$, a contradiction. \item If \underline{$w''=0$}, then $2a_4= u'' a_1+ v'' a_2$, and after substituting in here $a_4= 2a_2-ua_1$ (from \eqref{eq:case-b}) we get $$ (4-v'')a_2= (2u+u'')a_1. $$  egin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm, label*=\arabic*.] \item If \underline{$v''=0$}, then $a_4= u'' a_1/2$ and $u''$ is odd. Other generators are obtained immediately:  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=&  rac{2u+u''}{4} \cdot a_1, \ a_3 &=&  rac{4u'+2u''+v'(2u+u'')}{8} \cdot a_1. \ \end{eqnarray*} Since $u''$ is odd we deduce that $4|a_1$, hence $a_1 \in \{8,12 \}$. If \underline{$a_1=12$}, because the denominators of $a_2,a_3$ and $a_4$ are powers of $2$ we see that $a_2, a_3, a_4$ are divisible by $3$, and the same holds for $a_5$, a contradiction. \ 
oindent Assume \underline{$a_1=8$}. If $v'=0$ then we note that $a_2, a_3, a_4$ are even, hence $a_5$ is even, too. This is false. Hence $v'=1$, and the generators of the semigroup are  egin{eqnarray} a_1 &=& 8, 
onumber\ a_4 &=& 4u'', 
onumber \ a_2 &=& 4u+2u'', \ a_3 &=& 4u'+ 2u+ 3u'', 
onumber \ a_5 &=& 4u'+6u+ 9u''-8, 
onumber \end{eqnarray} which is on our list. \item If \underline{$v''=1$}, then $3a_2=(2u+u'') a_1$ which implies $3 
mid 2u+u''$ and $3|a_1$. We get  egin{eqnarray*} a_2 &=&  rac{2u+u''}{3} \cdot a_1, \ a_4 &=& 2a_2-u=  rac{2u''+u}{3} \cdot a_1. \end{eqnarray*} By \eqref{eq:sum} we see that $a_5=a_2+a_3+a_4-a_1= (u+u''-1) a_1+ a_3$, which is false. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: With $w'=1$ only $w''=0$, $v''=0$, $a_1=8$, $v'=1$ survives, giving the sixth and last family.

nodes.name: Conclusion of the long proof
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:5-quad-non-cm} is now complete. $\square$
nodes.statement_short: All cases exhausted, so Theorem 1.8 is proved.
